summary: Kearney Regional Airport (EAR) is a medium-sized regional airport serving the city of Kearney in south-central Nebraska. It supports both commercial passenger service and general aviation, playing a key role in connecting central Nebraska to larger hub airports. The airport features modernized facilities and is positioned near major highways, making it accessible to travelers throughout the region.
faqs:
Q: Where is Kearney Regional Airport located?
A: The airport is located in Kearney, Nebraska, just a few miles southeast of the city center near Highway 30 and Interstate 80.

Q: Does Kearney Regional Airport offer commercial flights?
A: Yes, it offers scheduled commercial passenger service, typically through regional carriers connecting to larger hub airports.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport features a passenger terminal, car rental services, parking areas, and general aviation amenities for private and charter flights.

Q: How large is the airport?
A: It is classified as a medium-sized regional airport with runways capable of handling a variety of commercial and general aviation aircraft.
transport_tips: Renting a car is the most convenient way to reach Kearney and the surrounding area, as the airport has rental agencies on-site. The airport is just a short drive from downtown Kearney via local roads, with easy access to Interstate 80 for travelers heading to other parts of Nebraska. Taxi and rideshare services may be limited, so arranging ground transportation in advance is recommended.
local_tip: If you have time before your flight, check out the Great Platte River Road Archway Monument just off Interstate 80 near Kearney, which tells the story of westward expansion along the Oregon Trail.
